sentences.text: Today we are going to talk about something very important, job interviews.
Going to a job interview in another language can be scary, but don't worry, in this episode
we will learn how to introduce yourself. Talk about your experience,
answer common interview questions, ask questions at the end of an interview,
use polite and professional English, show confidence in a job interview.
This episode is for A1 level English learners, so I will speak slowly and clearly.
Are you ready? Let's get started.
One, arriving at the interview. When you arrive for your job interview,
you may need to check in at the reception desk.
Common phrases. Hello, my name is Emi-Lee. I have an interview at 10am.
I am here for an interview with Mr. Smith. Where should I wait?
May I use the restroom before my interview?
Example dialogue. Hello, my name is Emi-Lee. I have an interview at 10am.
Thank you. Tip, arrive 10-15 minutes early for your interview to show that you are punctual.
Two, introducing yourself. At the beginning of the interview,
the interviewer will greet you and ask you to introduce yourself.
Common phrases. Hello, nice to meet you. Thank you for having me today.
I'm excited to be here. Example dialogue. Hello, welcome. My name is Mr. Johnson.
Nice to meet you. Nice to meet you too. Thank you for having me today.
How are you today? I'm doing well. Thank you. Tip, shake hands and smile when you greet the
interviewer. Three, talking about yourself. The interviewer will ask you to talk about yourself.
Common phrases. My name is Emi-Lee and I am from France.
I studied marketing at university. I have worked as a sales assistant for two years.
I love working with people. Example dialogue. Can you tell me a little about yourself?
Sure. My name is Emi-Lee and I am from France. I studied marketing at university
and I have worked as a sales assistant for two years. I enjoy working with people and helping
customers. Tip, keep your answer short and simple. Four, talking about your work experience.
The interviewer will ask about your work experience. Common phrases.
I worked as a cashier at a supermarket. I have experience in customer service.
I am good at communication. Example dialogue.
Interviewer. What experience do you have in this field? I worked as a cashier at a supermarket for
two years. I have experience in customer service and I am good at working in a team.
Tip, use past tense when talking about past jobs.
Answering common interview questions. The interviewer may ask basic questions.
Here are some examples. Common questions and answers.
Interviewer. Why do you want to work here? I want to work here because I like your company
and I enjoy helping customers. What are your strengths? I am friendly, hard working,
and a good team player. What are your weaknesses? Sometimes I am too detail oriented
but I am working on being faster. Tip, be positive, and confident in your answers.
Six, asking questions at the end. At the end of the interview, you can ask your own questions.
Common questions to ask the interviewer. What are the next steps in the hiring process?
What is a typical day like in this job? Can you tell me more about the team?
What are the opportunities for growth in this company?
Example dialogue. Emily. Thank you for the interview. What are the next steps?
We will contact you in a few days. Great. I look forward to hearing from you.
The interview. Seven, final tips for a successful interview.
Arrive on time. Dress professionally. Speak clearly and confidently. Smile and be friendly.
Prepare answers to common questions. Ask questions at the end. That's the end of today's episode.
I hope you feel more confident speaking English in a job interview.
